## Faster launch

- Resesh now shows its window in about a quarter of a second, down from about 0.8 seconds.
- The app is compiled to native code ahead of time, so nothing is compiled while it starts. It uses less CPU and memory at launch, and the download is about half the size.
- Settings and saved sessions load in the background while the window is created, and registering for notifications waits until the window is showing.

## Jump hosts, proxies and tunnels

- Reach a host behind a bastion: pick another saved SSH session as the jump host in the new Network section of the session editor. Jump hosts can be chained, and telnet sessions can use one too.
- Each jump host logs in with its own login and has its own host key check, asked for one host at a time as the connection reaches it.
- Or connect through a SOCKS5, SOCKS4 or HTTP proxy.
- Local, remote and dynamic (SOCKS) tunnels are saved with the session and open when it connects. The Tunnels dialog adds, stops and restarts tunnels on a connected tab, and shows why one failed.
- Bulk edit sets a jump host for many sessions at once. OpenSSH ProxyJump and PuTTY proxy settings come across on import.
- The file pane follows the jump host or proxy. Opening a folder in File Explorer does not yet.

Choose the x64 download for Intel or AMD PCs. Choose ARM64 only for Windows on ARM devices.
